messages.subject: help with plot margins
parts:
Dear all

I will like to understand how to use plot margins to increase/decrease margin text -- in particular the use of underlined code

c <- qplot(uempmed, unemploy, data = economics, geom="path")

csmall <- c + opts(plot.margin = unit(rep(0, 4), "lines"))

What is the use of unit function? and its "lines" argument ?

Also kindly advice where I can learn about plot margins in ggplot2

many thanks for your help

Regards
ravi

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: help with plot margins
parts:
Hi,

unit() is a function from the grid package that is used to specify the
size of graphical objects such as rectangles, viewports (=placeholders
where graphical objects may be drawn), etc. You can read its help page
from ?unit

unit() allows you to specify a size with a number of physical units
such as centimeters, inches, or "line" for instance. One "line" unit
is the height of a text line in the default font size, it is
particularly useful for specifying the spacing of the margins where we
might want to place axis labels, titles, etc.

The following function can illustrate graphically the effect of
changing the margin size; the second example shows that you can
specify each margin size independently (with different numbers and
units if necessary),

require(grid)

testMargins <- function(margins=unit(rep(1, 4), "lines")){
## the order is (bottom, left, top, right)
grid.newpage()
grid.rect(x=unit(c( 0.5, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9), "npc") -
unit.c( unit(0, "npc"), margins[2]*0.5, unit(0, "npc"),
-0.5*margins[4]),
y=unit(c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), "npc") -
unit.c(margins[1]*0.5, unit(0, "npc"), -0.5*margins[3],
unit(0, "npc")),
width=unit.c(unit(0.8, "npc"), margins[2], unit(0.8,
"npc"), margins[4]),
height=unit.c(margins[1], unit(0.8, "npc"), margins[3],
unit(0.8, "npc")))

grid.text(paste("margin", 1:4, "\n(", as.character(margins), ")"),
x=unit(c( 0.5, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9), "npc") -
unit.c( unit(0, "npc"), margins[2]*0.5, unit(0,
"npc"), -0.5*margins[4]),
y=unit(c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), "npc") -
unit.c(margins[1]*0.5, unit(0, "npc"),
-0.5*margins[3], unit(0, "npc")),
rot=c(0, 90, 0, 90))

}
testMargins()

testMargins(unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0), c("cm", "in", "line", "npc")))


HTH,

baptiste
